Definition: to be (or make) clean (literally or figuratively); by implication (in an adverse sense) to be bare, i.e. extirpated
BiblicalUsage: Naqah means to be clean or clear, to be held guiltless, and it is the word for innocence before God and before men. In Genesis 24:8 Abraham's servant is told he shall be clear from the oath if the woman will not follow, and in Exodus 20:7 the Lord will not hold him guiltless who takes His name in vain. In Numbers 14:18 the Lord is longsuffering and forgiving, and by no means clearing the guilty, and in Psalm 19:12 David asks God to cleanse him from secret faults.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being clear is the question every conscience asks, because the servant wants to be clear of his oath and David wants to be clear of his secret faults. God clears the guilty only through forgiveness, and He never clears the guilty without it. I hold that my clearance is in the mercy of Numbers 14:18, not in my own record.
